title: South African municipal water-service / procurement source discovery register
purpose: Record public source candidates and explicit unknowns before selecting a municipality, case cohort, or benchmark label.

scope.candidate_domain: municipal water-service repair and associated procurement

sources.name: National Treasury eTender Transparency Portal
sources.owner: South African National Treasury / Office of the Chief Procurement Officer
sources.reported_temporal_coverage: Monthly detailed downloads from May 2021; verify each selected file and its actual rows.
sources.reported_license: Official portal says detailed monthly downloads are CC BY 4.0; re-check terms for each exact artifact and derived output.
known_caveats: Portal states the published data cover only a subset of public procurement captured by eTender.
Absence from the published dataset is not evidence that a procurement did not occur.
The existence of a tender, award, or contract does not prove that work was delivered or a service outcome improved.
Record-level completeness, amendment coverage, stable join keys, and selected-cohort accuracy have not been validated.
sources.intended_use: Reconstruct the published procurement chronology and identify candidates for independent review.

sources.name: National Treasury Municipal Finance Data / Municipal Money API
sources.owner: South African National Treasury, with OpenUp as a public-data partner
sources.reported_temporal_coverage: Financial years 2008-09 through 2025-26; portal reports latest 2026 Q2 data on the discovery date.
sources.reported_scope: 292 municipalities, with more than 85 million reported facts according to the portal.
known_caveats: Portal says completeness and integrity checks are in progress.
The data are only as complete and trustworthy as municipal submissions.
Blank/not-submitted values must not be interpreted as zero.
Municipal financial performance cannot by itself establish water repair completion, service reliability, or corruption.
sources.intended_use: Contextualize budgets and expenditure; corroborate amounts only after matching definitions, periods, and identifiers.

sources.name: Department of Water and Sanitation National Integrated Water Information System (NIWIS)
sources.owner: South African Department of Water and Sanitation
sources.reported_scope: Dashboard themes include Water Services, Sanitation Services, Water Quality, Water Quantity, monitoring networks, and related water information.
known_caveats: Stable raw-data export/API availability has not been confirmed.
Municipality/location resolution, time frequency, latency, definitions, and historical depth have not been profiled.
An aggregate dashboard indicator may not be granular enough to validate a specific repair episode.
Dashboard presentation is not independent verification by itself.
sources.intended_use: Candidate outcome/context source only if series definitions, time/location resolution, and reuse terms pass the audit.

required_evidence_classes.description: Original dated public commitment, target definition, budget, responsible authority, and revision rules.
Tender, award, contract/amendment, and (where available) payment evidence with identifiers and history.
Budgeted/actual expenditure with reporting period and measure definition.
Independently corroborated, location/time-aligned water-service restoration, reliability, or quality observation.
Privacy-preserving channel for residents or service users to submit counterevidence and contest status.

linkage_candidates_to_verify: project or site identifier and geospatial resolution
tender, award, contract, amendment, payment, and service-event dates
measurement units, denominators, missingness codes, and source revisions
whether a service observation actually covers the claimed repair location and period
audit_checklist: pin exact source URL, retrieval timestamp, file/API version, license, bytes, and digest
profile schemas, row counts, keys, duplicates, nulls, and unexplained time gaps
measure municipality-period coverage before selecting a case cohort
verify publication and correction histories; keep missing, suppressed, stale, and measured-zero states distinct
compute linkage rates and retain unresolved joins as unknown
manually compare a prespecified sample against original documents and independent evidence
document source ownership, dependencies, and whether sources are genuinely independent
review privacy, retaliation, POPIA, license, and safe-publication constraints
freeze eligibility rules before inspecting which municipalities or officials appear favorable or unfavorable
go_no_go_rules: Do not infer nonexistence from an absent eTender record because portal coverage is partial.
Do not infer service completion from a tender award, contract, payment, or budget line alone.
Do not call finance, procurement, and water dashboard values corroborating evidence until their temporal/identifier alignment and source independence are established.
Do not label corruption from anomalies alone; allegations, anomaly flags, procedural violations, and adjudicated findings remain different states.

If independently corroborated service outcomes cannot be obtained, do not claim the pilot measures service-delivery impact; narrow to an explicitly labeled data-integrity study or choose another domain.
Do not select a named municipality or publish case-level allegations before coverage, legal-use, privacy, and labeling rules are frozen.
next_actions: Fetch one dated sample export/API response from each candidate source and preserve exact artifact bytes and retrieval metadata.
Build a municipality-period-source coverage matrix before choosing any cohort.
Check whether procurement identifiers join to project locations and whether any suitable independent water-outcome time series exists.
If coverage is insufficient, document the gap and stop or change domains instead of imputing ground truth.
